comments.headline: Overhead distribution clearance violations and missing Austin Energy approval
comments.summary: Trees occupy prohibited clearance zones from the overhead distribution line and utility poles. Run 1 confirmed violations for non-utility-compatible species and pole proximity. However, species identification, mature height documentation, and clearance dimensions are missing, hindering full verification. No documented Austin Energy approval exists for trees in restricted zones.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy (for approval of restricted-zone tree placement)
comments.attn: Clarify which trees are proposed in restricted zones. If trees remain in restricted zones, obtain written Austin Energy approval.

details.text: Non-utility-compatible Live Oak (not designated UC in ECM Appendix F) is proposed within 15 lateral feet of the overhead distribution conductor. Tree must be relocated beyond 15 feet or documented Austin Energy approval provided.

runComments.comment: Non-utility-compatible trees (Live Oak) are proposed within 15 lateral feet of the overhead electric distribution line. No clearance dimensions or Austin Energy approvals are provided. Live Oak (Quercus virginiana) is not marked as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F and is therefore prohibited within 15 feet of distribution conductors. Applicant must either relocate the Live Oak trees beyond 15 feet of the OHE line or provide documented Austin Energy written approval for the exception.

Trees marked as 'M' (Mitigation) and 'P' (Parking Buffer) are positioned 5-10 feet from the overhead electric (OHE) line on the landscape plan, which falls within the < 15 lateral feet distribution restriction zone requiring utility-compatible species only. However, the landscape plan does not identify which specific species are labeled with these symbols, and the plant list on Sheet 35 does not indicate which of the four proposed shade/ornamental species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are the 'M' and 'P' trees. Without species identification linked to tree symbol locations, and without ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designations, compliance cannot be verified.

Overhead electric distribution line (OHE) is present on the site. Proposed tree species are listed on Sheet 35 (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but utility-compatible (UC) status cannot be verified from submitted documents as ECM Appendix F is not included. Additionally, no clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan to verify whether any non-utility-compatible trees are within the required 15-foot lateral distance from the distribution conductor.

details.text: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet, such as Live Oak) are proposed within 25 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors. Tree must be relocated beyond 25 feet or documented Austin Energy approval provided.

runComments.comment: Large trees (Live Oak, mature height 40+ feet) are proposed within 25 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductors. No clearance dimensions, spacing requirements, or Austin Energy written approval are documented. Applicant must either relocate the Live Oak trees to greater than 25 feet from the distribution conductors or provide documented Austin Energy written approval for the exception.

Trees are positioned within 25 feet of the overhead electric line. The requirement prohibits large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) within this zone. However, the landscape plan does not differentiate which trees are 'large trees' (40+ feet mature height). Sheet 35 lists species with their container size specifications but does not document mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Without mature height documentation linked to tree locations on the plan, compliance cannot be verified.

Proposed tree species list does not include mature height specifications. Sheet 35 provides minimum container sizes (100 gal., 45 gal.) and caliper inches (4", 2.5") but not the mature heights required to determine which trees are 'large trees' (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Without mature height data and clearance dimensions, compliance with the 25-foot distribution clearance requirement for large trees cannot be verified.

details.text: Trees are proposed within 10 lateral feet of utility poles on the overhead electric line. At least one mitigation tree on the southeastern boundary is positioned within approximately 10 feet of a utility pole. Tree must be relocated beyond 10 feet (measured from trunk center to pole structure).

runComments.comment: Trees are proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead electric utility poles. At least one mitigation tree shown on the landscape plan is positioned within approximately 10 feet of a utility pole on the southeastern property boundary. The tree must be relocated to greater than 10 feet from the pole, measured from tree trunk center to pole structure.

Overhead electric poles are shown on the landscape plan as circular symbols with 'x' marks along the OHE line on the southern boundary. Trees marked 'M' and 'P' are positioned 5-10 feet from the OHE line. The requirement prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of utility poles. However, the landscape plan does not provide exact dimensions from tree trunk centers to pole centerlines, and the 'M' and 'P' tree species are not identified on the plan. Without exact measurements and species identification, compliance cannot be verified.

Utility pole symbols are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and site plan (Sheet 9) along the OHE line, but their exact locations are not dimensioned. Proposed tree locations are shown but no clearance dimensions are provided from trees to the poles. Therefore, the 10-foot lateral clearance requirement cannot be verified.

details.text: No documented written approval from Austin Energy has been provided for trees proposed in prohibited clearance zones (within 15 feet of distribution conductors, within 25 feet for large trees, within 10 feet of utility poles).

runComments.comment: Trees are proposed within prohibited clearance zones from overhead electric facilities (within 15 feet of distribution conductors, within 25 feet for large trees, and within 10 feet of utility poles) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Applicant must either relocate the violating trees outside restricted zones or provide explicit written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the exception. Letters or approvals should be attached to the site plan or submitted as supplementary documentation.

Trees are positioned within restricted clearance zones (5-10 feet from the OHE line and utility poles along the southern boundary). The plans do not provide evidence of Austin Energy written approval for these placements. No approval letters, correspondence, or notes in the submitted site plan documents indicate that Austin Energy has authorized the tree placement in these restricted zones. If trees within prohibited zones are proposed, documented written approval from Austin Energy must be provided on or attached to the site plan.

Cannot determine whether any trees are proposed within prohibited clearance zones without: (1) species identification with UC status verification against ECM Appendix F, (2) mature height identification to determine if trees are large (40+ feet), (3) clearance dimensions from trees to conductors and equipment. Therefore, it cannot be determined whether Austin Energy written approval is required.

comments.headline: Tree species and mature height documentation missing; clearance dimensions not shown
comments.summary: Tree symbols on the landscape plan show only functional labels (M, P, SY, PL) without species identification or mature heights. Plant schedule lists species but lacks mature height documentation per ECM Appendix F and species-to-location cross-reference. Clearance dimensions from trees to electrical facilities are not shown. Without this documentation, utility-compatibility and large-tree distinction (40+ feet) cannot be verified.
comments.attn: Provide clear plant legend on landscape plan linking tree symbols to species names and mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Add dimension lines from tree trunk centers to overhead electric line, utility poles, and underground equipment locations.

details.text: Landscape plan labels trees with functional designations ('M', 'P', 'SY', 'PL') but does not identify botanical or common names. Plant list on Sheet 35 specifies four species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) but does not cross-reference which species correspond to which symbols on the drawing. Reviewer must manually correlate species to locations across multiple sheets.

runComments.comment: Trees proposed near the overhead electric line on the landscape plan are labeled with functional designations ('M' for Mitigation, 'P' for Parking Buffer) but the landscape plan does not directly identify the botanical or common names of these specific trees. The plant list on Sheet 35 specifies species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) but does not cross-reference which species are labeled 'M' or 'P' on the actual drawing. A reviewer must reference multiple sheets and cannot directly correlate tree symbols on the landscape plan to specific species. Provide a clear plant legend on the landscape plan that identifies the species of each labeled tree, or clearly reference the plant schedule with species names linked to drawing symbols.

The landscape plan (Sheet 31) uses abbreviation codes to label tree locations (M = Mitigation Tree, SY = Street Yard Tree, PL = Parking Lot Tree, P = Parking Buffer Point Tree) but provides no legend on that sheet correlating these codes to the specific botanical names. The plant schedule with species identification is located on a separate sheet (Sheet 35). A reader cannot determine which species is planted at which location on the landscape plan without cross-referencing multiple sheets.

details.text: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) from smaller species through notation, color-coding, legend, or labeling. Plant schedule on Sheet 35 provides container specifications and caliper sizes but does not document mature heights for any proposed species.

runComments.comment: Large trees (40+ feet mature height) are not visually differentiated on the landscape plan. All tree symbols appear identical regardless of mature height. Applicant should modify the landscape plan to specifically label or differentiate large trees (such as Live Oak at 40+ feet) to facilitate verification of clearances from electric facilities. This can be accomplished through unique symbols, labels, or callout notes on the landscape plan.

The landscape plan does not differentiate or designate large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) from smaller trees. Tree symbols on the plan are marked by functional category ('M', 'P', 'SY', 'PL') but include no notation, color-coding, or legend entry identifying which trees are 'large' (≥40 feet mature height). The plant schedule on Sheet 35 does not document mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Large trees positioned within 25 feet of overhead distribution facilities require specific clearance compliance; without identification of large trees on the plan, such compliance cannot be verified. Provide a clear designation (notation, color, legend symbol) on the landscape plan identifying trees with mature heights of 40 feet or greater per ECM Appendix F.

The landscape plan does not indicate mature heights for any of the proposed trees. Sheet 35 provides minimum container specifications and caliper sizes but does not specify the mature height for any tree species. Without mature height information on or cross-referenced to the landscape plan, large trees (those with mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) cannot be differentiated from smaller trees, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance for large trees from overhead electric facilities.

details.text: Landscape plan lacks dimension lines or measurements from tree trunk centers to the overhead electric line, utility poles, or between conductors and pole centerlines. Without dimensional evidence, the measurement method (pole centerline versus outside conductor position) cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan does not provide dimension lines or measurements from tree trunk centers to the overhead electric line or from the OHE line to utility poles. While pole symbols are shown on the OHE line, no dimensions or calculations are provided to demonstrate that clearances are measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline). Without dimensional evidence on the plan, the measurement methodology cannot be verified.

No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan from trees to the overhead electric conductor or poles. Because no dimensions are present, the method of measurement (whether from pole centerline versus conductor, whether from trunk center versus canopy edge) cannot be evaluated. If clearance dimensions were to be added to the plan, they must originate from the outside conductor position, not pole centerline.

details.text: No dimension lines or measurements from tree locations are provided on the landscape plan. Without dimensional documentation, it cannot be determined whether any distance measurements (if shown elsewhere) originate from tree trunk centers (correct per requirement) or projected canopy edges (incorrect).

runComments.comment: The landscape plan does not provide dimension lines or measurements from tree locations. Without dimensioned evidence showing whether measurements originate at tree trunk centers (planting locations) or at projected canopy edges, the measurement methodology cannot be verified.

No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan. Because dimensions are absent, it cannot be determined whether any dimensions that may exist elsewhere originate from tree trunk centers (correct) or tree canopy edges (incorrect). Proper clearance measurement must originate from tree trunk center (planting location).

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) do not clearly cross-reference or align. Reviewer must manually verify that all overhead conductors and poles shown on the electrical plan are depicted on the landscape plan relative to proposed tree locations.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows the overhead electric (OHE) line and poles along the southern boundary. However, the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows only underground electrical infrastructure; the two plans do not clearly cross-reference or align. While the OHE line is present on the landscape plan, a reviewer must cross-reference between sheets to verify that all overhead conductors and poles are depicted on the landscape plan. The electrical plan should be referenced or overlaid on the landscape plan to provide complete clarity on overhead facility locations and ensure all conductors are shown relative to tree locations.

While the overhead electric line (OHE) is shown on the landscape plan and tree symbols are present, the plans do not provide sufficient information to verify clearances. Specifically: (1) no dimension lines or distance measurements are provided from trees to the OHE conductor; (2) the tree symbols on the landscape plan are not identified by species (only by functional category: M, SY, PL), so utility-compatibility cannot be assessed; (3) utility pole locations are shown graphically but not dimensioned. The lack of dimensional cross-reference and species identification prevents verification that trees comply with required clearance distances from overhead electric facilities.

comments.headline: Underground electrical equipment clearances and root barriers not documented
comments.summary: Electrical design plan shows underground equipment but does not distinguish pad-mounted items. Landscape plan lacks overlay of underground equipment locations with trees, preventing verification of 5-foot clearance requirements. Root barrier specifications (4 feet deep, 5 feet from equipment) for trees within 20 feet are not documented.
comments.crossDep: Electrical design (coordinate sheet overlays and equipment identification)
comments.attn: Clarify pad-mounted equipment locations. Overlay electrical plan with landscape plan. Specify root barrier details for trees within 20 feet of underground equipment.

details.text: Electrical design plan does not clearly distinguish pad-mounted equipment from other electrical elements (transformers, pull boxes, meters). Landscape plan does not show electrical equipment locations in relation to proposed trees. Compliance with 10-foot clearance requirement from pad-mounted equipment cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, electrical meters) but does not clearly distinguish pad-mounted equipment from other electrical elements. The landscape plan does not show electrical equipment locations in relation to proposed trees. Therefore, compliance with the 10-foot clearance requirement from pad-mounted equipment cannot be verified.

details.text: Underground electrical equipment locations (per Sheet 21) are not clearly indicated on the landscape plan in relation to proposed trees. Electrical design plan and landscape plan are not overlaid or cross-referenced, preventing verification that trees maintain required 5-foot distance from underground equipment.

runComments.comment: Underground electric equipment locations are not clearly indicated on the landscape plan in relation to proposed trees. Applicant should show underground equipment locations and identify any trees within 5 lateral feet of such equipment.

Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical elements but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay electrical equipment locations with proposed tree locations. Clearance dimensions from trees to underground equipment are not shown. The 5-foot lateral clearance requirement cannot be verified from the submitted plans.

details.text: Root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) required for trees within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment are not shown on the landscape plan. Clearance dimensions from trees to underground equipment are absent, preventing determination of whether any trees fall within the 20-foot threshold requiring root barriers.

runComments.comment: Cannot verify whether root barriers are specified for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Applicant should show underground equipment locations on the landscape plan and specify root barrier requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) for any trees within 20 feet.

While underground electrical equipment is shown on Sheet 21, the landscape plan does not provide root barrier specifications or details. No clearance dimensions are shown from trees to underground equipment to determine whether any trees fall within the 20-foot threshold requiring root barriers. Root barrier requirements therefore cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Transmission infrastructure and easement boundaries not identified on plans
comments.summary: Landscape plan does not identify transmission facilities, locations, or easement boundaries, preventing verification of 50-foot transmission conductor clearances and easement tree prohibitions. Applicant must clarify whether transmission infrastructure is present and, if so, depict all transmission lines, structures, and easement boundaries on landscape and grading plans.
comments.attn: Confirm whether transmission infrastructure is present on the property. If present, provide transmission easement boundaries, structure locations, and clearance dimensions on all applicable sheets.

details.text: Transmission facilities, easement locations, and structure positions are not clearly identified on the landscape plan. Verification of compliance with 50-foot transmission conductor clearance requirements cannot be completed without transmission infrastructure locations depicted.

runComments.comment: Cannot verify whether transmission facilities are present or the location and extent of transmission easements. The landscape plan does not clearly identify transmission infrastructure or easement boundaries, preventing verification of compliance with 50-foot transmission conductor clearance requirements. Applicant should clarify whether transmission facilities are present and, if so, show transmission easement boundaries and structure locations on the landscape plan.

details.text: Large trees (40+ feet mature height) positioned within 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors cannot be verified without identification and location of transmission infrastructure. Transmission facility locations are not shown on the landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Cannot verify whether large trees (40+ feet) are positioned within 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors due to unclear identification of transmission infrastructure and easement boundaries on the landscape plan. Applicant should clarify transmission facility locations if present.

details.text: Transmission easement boundaries are not depicted on the landscape plan, grading plan, or plat. Trees cannot be verified as positioned outside transmission easements without clear delineation of easement areas. If transmission facilities are present, easement boundaries must be shown on all relevant plan sheets per UCM § 1.14.6.

runComments.comment: Transmission easement boundaries are not clearly shown on the landscape plan, grading plan, or plat. Without depicted easement areas, it cannot be verified that trees are positioned outside transmission easements. Applicant must show transmission easement boundaries on all relevant plan sheets if transmission facilities are present on the property.
